intent.note:
Clause: 'Drop the parent's Claude session variables (CLAUDECODE and every CLAUDE_CODE_* / CLAUDE_EFFORT; keep any CLAUDE_* the runner sets on purpose and name them)'. The diff drops by rule: PARENT_SESSION_VARS holds CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_PID, CLAUDE_EFFORT, AUDIT_LOCK_TOKENS and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR. PARENT_SESSION_PREFIXES=('CLAUDE_CODE_',) drops every name in that namespace. _is_parent_session_var exempts the named provider and credential switches (KEEP_SESSION_VARS, KEEP_SESSION_PREFIXES). The runner sets no CLAUDE_* variable of its own, so naming none matches the clause. That scope is the one the clause asked for; the closed-list narrowing is gone. The executor's outcome describes the diff: constants, helper, docstring and comment edits, ras30b and ras30c added. Dependants: PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md still resolves PARENT_SESSION_VARS, but its 'the list the plain arm unsets' wording is stale (finding 3). The other listed files do not use the env constants. In this diff, grep for PARENT_SESSION_VARS or _session_env finds only the runner and the guide. The one run I did of `python3 tests/test_run_agent_session.py --selftest` ended ALL PASS: 37/37 cases, exit 0.

Extra question, is dropping CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR from the child correct? Yes. It was already in the list at HEAD, and this diff keeps it. A plain top-level session started from a shell does not carry it; the CLI sets it for its own hooks. The runner starts the child with cwd=tree (the task's worktree). hooks/_config.py repo_root() lets CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR win over cwd (line 467), so an inherited orchestrator value would point the child's config lookup at the orchestrator's project instead of the task tree. Dropping it makes the child resolve from its own cwd, as a plain session does. Residual risk: I did not observe whether the CLI overwrites an inherited value; either way, dropping is safe.
